messages:
maria: quick sync — proposing a small infra primitive: 'hedge-proxy' to manage A/B canaries and automated fallback. idea: lightweight reverse-proxy that tracks per-variant latency and error signals and can transparently route/hedge/fallback without touching app code.
aj: sounds useful. curious how it differs from existing router + circuit-breaker we have.
simon: main difference is decentralized per-route short-memory telemetry + ttl-based trial windows. hedge-proxy keeps tiny windowed histograms per (tenant, route, variant) and can make immediate routing decisions.
maria: exactly. design goals: zero schema changes for clients, consistent fail-open semantics, bounded memory, deterministic probe scheduling, and a visible decision trace in logs.
tara: what signals are we using? p50/p95 latency, errors, incomplete streams? any model-quality signals?
maria: primary: 5xx/error rate, tail latency (p95), and probe-failed count. model-quality not in the proxy — that's app-level. proxy exposes hooks so upper-layer can attach quality feedback if needed.
eli: how do we avoid flip-flop during noisy spikes?
maria: two layers: 1) debounce window (configurable 30–120s), 2) hysteresis via token bucket -> only allow N switches per minute. plus a short cool-down after fallback.
simon: we should also tag decisions with a 'confidence' score derived from sample size. low-sample changes go into a 'dry-run' route (mirror) first.
maria: yep. plan: dry-run (mirror traffic) -> shadow + metrics compare -> staged ramp -> hedge -> fallback. fallback path is deterministic and can be chosen by policy (owner-defined): 'stable', 'last-good', 'regional' etc.
aj: ops question: where does KV live? we can't store huge histograms in-host.
maria: store compact stats in in-memory LRU with periodic flush to durable store for longer analysis (prometheus as metrics + tiny redis for checksums). histograms are t-digest-ish compressed.
tara: config example?
maria: ```
proxy.rules:
  - route: /v1/generate
    policy:
      default_variant: stable-v2
      allowed_variants: [stable-v2, canary-v3]
      trial_window: 60s
      max_switches_per_min: 2
      fallback: stable-v2
      mirror_for_dry_run: true
``
eli: rollback triggers? automated fallback should be reversible if canary recovers, right?
maria: yes: two thresholds — critical (immediate fallback) and recover (gradual re-introduction). also manual override in console.
deploy-bot: deploy started for patch/infra/hedge-proxy v0.1 -> rolling across infra-edge-1..3 :rocket:
ops-bot: alert-rule-suggestion: create composite alert if (canary_error_rate > 2% && p95_increase > 2x) for 30s.
simon: telemetry contract: proxy emits decision events to a lightweight kafka topic: {route,variant,decision,reason,confidence,window_start,window_end}. also emits aggregated metrics to prometheus.
tara: how will this interact with Dedicated customers who manage their own routing?
maria: offer two modes: sidecar (per-customer) and network-proxy (platform-managed). sidecar runs with local config and writes events to customer topics. network-proxy can be tenant-aware and respect privacy boundaries.
eli: perf overhead?
maria: p75 added latency measured in local perf tests: ~0.6–1.2ms for simple pass-through; hedging adds additional calls but we can opt-in per-route. quantization: sample-based mirroring to avoid cost explosion.
aj: ops runbook note: on mass failure, proxy should expose an escape hatch env var (REDWOOD_PROXY_FAIL_OPEN=true) and a kill-switch that flips all canaries to fallback.
maria: next steps: RFC PR with state machine, metrics contract, and a small PoC in k8s (sidecar). i'll draft an RFC by EOD. comments?
simon: add a paragraph about privacy: ensure no request body stored in logs, only hashes and decision metadata.
maria: agreed. i'll include that.
tara: :thumbsup: small nit — add tenant-rate limiting interaction so fallback doesn't cause overload on stable variant.
maria: good catch, will address with admission checks.
eli: happy to pair on the PoC tomorrow.
maria: thanks all. will post RFC link shortly. :wave:
